result.effect: All pairwise correlations >0.50; MAP correlations 0.78-0.83 with ACCESS, DIBELS, and TRC-English, and 0.65 with TRC-Spanish

cells.quote:
All of the assessments are positively correlated with each other, surpassing the 0.50 threshold of a moderate relationship, and many are highly correlated, surpassing a 0.70 threshold of a strong relationship.
The MAP shows the strongest correlations with the other assessments, ranging from 0.78 to 0.83 with each of the other assessments (ACCESS, DIBELS, and TRC-English), except TRC-Spanish, where the correlation is 0.65.
cells.note: The contrast is between assessment pairs with stronger versus weaker observed associations; no assessment was manipulated.

result.effect: Correlations with third-grade assessment scores ranged from 0.67 to 0.82; individual assessments were generally slightly less predictive than latent scores

cells.quote:
Most of the assessments, and the combined latent scores, are highly predictive of third grade assessment scores in pre-pandemic years, with correlations ranging from 0.67 (kindergarten latent score predicting third grade PARCC/IAR score) to 0.82 (second grade latent score predicting third grade MAP score).
Almost all the individual assessments are moderately-to-highly predictive of third grade assessment scores, although slightly less predictive than the latent scores.
cells.note: This is a comparison of predictive associations, not a randomized treatment effect.

result.effect: Correlations ranged from 0.52 in kindergarten to 0.63 in second grade; TRC-Spanish was not correlated in pre-pandemic cohorts

cells.quote:

TRC-Spanish scores are not correlated with students’ third grade ELA grades in pre-pandemic cohorts.
cells.note: The result is mixed because MAP and latent scores were predictive, other assessments were somewhat weaker, and TRC-Spanish showed no relationship in pre-pandemic cohorts.
